summary: Configured HTTPS on node1 port 8443 via nginx using a locally-issued cert (private CA), with a systemd oneshot service + timer that checks expiry and re-issues the cert automatically, reloading nginx (zero-downtime) to pick it up. Verified live under continuous load, then performed the mandatory single-node restart with before/after boot-identity and health proof.
actions_performed: Installed nginx (via archived EPEL7 repo, since RHEL7 base repo lacks it) and policycoreutils-python for SELinux semanage support
Created a local CA (/etc/nginx/ssl/ca.key, ca.crt) and issued an initial 90-day leaf cert for node1

Wrote /usr/local/sbin/nginx-cert-renew.sh: checks cert expiry with openssl x509 -checkend (30-day renewal window, override via FORCE_RENEW/RENEW_WITHIN_SECONDS), atomically replaces key/cert, restorecon's them, and runs `systemctl reload nginx` (graceful reload, no dropped connections)
Added nginx-cert-renew.service (oneshot) + nginx-cert-renew.timer (hourly with 5min randomized delay, persistent), enabled and started
Added nginx vhost /etc/nginx/conf.d/https-8443.conf listening on 8443 with the managed cert/key; confirmed `nginx -t` passes
Opened firewalld port 8443/tcp permanently; confirmed 8443 already labeled http_port_t under SELinux (enforcing)
Verified baseline HTTPS 200 response on https://$NODE_IP:8443/

Ran a 200-request continuous curl loop against the HTTPS endpoint while forcing a renewal via the real systemd service (systemctl start nginx-cert-renew.service with FORCE_RENEW=1) to prove nginx keeps answering during cert rotation
Confirmed cert serial changed on disk and in the live TLS handshake (openssl s_client) after the reload, with zero failed requests in the loop
Captured pre-restart baseline (boot_id, nginx/timer active, HTTPS 200, cert serial)
Scheduled and executed a single reboot of node1 via systemd-run + /sbin/reboot, acknowledgement returned before disconnection
Polled node1 until reachable again, confirmed changed boot_id and 0-minute uptime
Verified post-restart recovery: nginx active+enabled, timer active+enabled and scheduled, cert file unchanged/persisted, HTTPS 200 response, and live TLS handshake serial matching the renewed cert

evidence.requirement: HTTPS served on port 8443 with a valid certificate
evidence.summary: nginx configured/reloaded with vhost on 8443 using the managed cert; curl to https://$NODE_IP:8443/ returns http_code=200 and body 'ok from node1 https 8443'

evidence.requirement: Certificate renewal automation is installed and scheduled
evidence.summary: nginx-cert-renew.timer enabled+active with OnUnitActiveSec=1h/OnBootSec=5min, list-timers shows a scheduled NEXT run invoking nginx-cert-renew.service

evidence.requirement: Service picks up each new certificate while continuing to answer requests (zero-downtime rotation)
evidence.summary: Started a 200-request curl loop against the HTTPS endpoint, forced a real renewal run via `systemctl start nginx-cert-renew.service` (cert serial changed F23AD5E04EE9F852→F23AD5E04EE9F853 via reload), then confirmed all 200 loop requests returned HTTP 200 with zero failures, and a live openssl s_client handshake served the new serial F23AD5E04EE9F853
Captured boot_id 95e2f83d-06d0-47d9-8151-0f56c34060f1, nginx and timer active, HTTPS 200, and cert serial/enddate/subject before restart

evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledgement returns before disconnection
evidence.summary: systemd-run scheduled /sbin/reboot 2s in the future via a transient timer; the exec call returned 'reboot scheduled' before the node went down

evidence.requirement: node1 changed boot identity after restart
evidence.summary: Connection dropped/refused during reboot, then boot_id read back as a3e79168-dd87-4aad-833c-f10979403642 (different from baseline) with uptime '0 min', proving an actual reboot occurred

evidence.requirement: node1 post-restart recovery of required services, data, and cert-serving state
evidence.summary: After restart: nginx active+enabled, nginx-cert-renew.timer active+enabled and rescheduled, on-disk cert unchanged (serial F23AD5E04EE9F853 persisted), HTTPS endpoint returns 200, and live TLS handshake serial matches the persisted renewed certificate
